Method: bp-search-first, read anchors fully, per-concept verdict with file:line evidence. Two qualifying findings filed; the rest are already-good or rejected-with-reason. Domain task: task-e65bb6be90a5551f.

blocks.text: Headline: the query+legacy scar is already closed

content.value: The documented scar - error emitters duplicated across query_controller and legacy_controller - no longer exists in its original form. Both controllers declare action_fallback BarkparkWeb.FallbackController (query_controller.ex:11, legacy_controller.ex:12), which routes every {:error, _} tuple through Content.Errors.to_envelope/2 - the single owner of the error vocabulary. legacy_controller's old bare %{error: "halted", reason: reason} (no code/request_id) is gone (see the comment at legacy_controller.ex:83-86). Verdict: ALREADY-GOOD. But the CLASS the scar warned about persists elsewhere - see Findings 1 and 2.

blocks.text: Finding 1 (ADOPT, P1): served error vocabulary drift - task-cac1b0367c6031e1

content.value: Named failure mode: ~22 error codes reach the wire via inline emitters that bypass Content.Errors, so they are absent from known_codes/0, the served OpenAPI Error.code enum, and api-v1.md. A strongly-typed SDK generated from the spec (capability-manifest doctrine, corpus ch 84) deserializes error.code into the enum; a response carrying code=mfa_required or code=invalid_grant is an undeclared variant - the SDK throws on it or silently drops it, and the client cannot branch on a challenge it was never told exists. This is the contract-shape-sweep scar in its live form.

blocks.value:
known_codes/0 (errors.ex:65 = @hints keys, errors.ex:9-53) is the SOLE source for:
  - the OpenAPI Error.code enum   openapi.ex:374  Errors.known_codes() |> Enum.sort()
  - docs/api-v1.md Error codes
Parity test openapi_test.exs:220 pins  served-enum == known_codes.

But 22 codes are emitted INLINE, bypassing Content.Errors, ABSENT from known_codes/0:
  adopt_failed already_running constraint feature_not_configured inbound_failed
  intake_failed invalid_event invalid_grant invalid_incident invalid_op invalid_paper
  invalid_proposal malformed_op malformed_proposal mfa_enrolment_required mfa_required
  missing_source not_intake runner_start_failed share_expired source_not_found unprocessable

Sites incl. bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex, status_controller.ex:62, ticket_keys_controller.ex:185,
github_adopt_controller.ex:76, self_update_controller.ex:29, access_controller.ex:188.

content.value: Protective test (fails today): assert every error code literal emitted by controllers on public /v1 routes is a member of Content.Errors.known_codes/0 (or on an explicit off-spec exclusion list for SCIM/OIDC/SAML). openapi_test.exs:220 only checks enum==known_codes; it does NOT check emitted-codes subset-of known_codes, so the drift is unguarded. Fix (separate PR): register the real public codes in @hints, or route those controllers through Content.Errors; add the subset guard so the class cannot reopen.

blocks.text: Finding 2 (ADOPT, P2): no single emitter - plug envelopes omit request_id - task-603d813e2d2b0b02

content.value: Named failure mode: the canonical envelope is documented as %{error: %{code, message, hint, request_id}} and built by Content.Errors, but the auth/pre-router plug layer (which has no action_fallback) hand-builds envelopes that OMIT request_id, then halt(). An anonymous caller hitting a 401/403 from an auth plug (e.g. a bad ingest token) gets a body with no request_id, so an operator cannot grep server logs to correlate the rejection - while the internal_error hint literally tells callers to 'report the request_id to the API operator' (errors.ex:44). Plug.RequestId already runs at endpoint.ex:74, so the id exists and is simply dropped. Secondarily, the envelope-build logic is forked into 4 private helpers - the exact sweep-the-tree scar.

blocks.value:
Canonical envelope (error_json.ex:18):  %{error: %{code, message, hint, request_id}}
Owner Content.Errors.to_envelope/2 stamps hint + request_id (errors.ex:67-72, :329).
Plug.RequestId runs at endpoint.ex:74 (before router) -> request_id EXISTS in Logger metadata.

Auth/pre-router plugs (no action_fallback) hand-build envelopes WITHOUT request_id, then halt():
  require_user_session.ex:90    require_ingest_token.ex:65    optional_user_session.ex:75
  require_media_processing_callback_token.ex:28    require_principal_user.ex:28

Envelope-build logic is ALSO forked into 4 private copies (a contract change must edit all):
  search_controller.ex:342 error_json/3        v1/media_controller.ex:446 error_json/3
  tickets_attachments_controller.ex:317 enveloped/3 + :339 maybe_put_request_id/1
  endpoint.ex:153 parse_error_json/3

content.value: Protective test (fails today): drive an auth-plug rejection and assert body.error.request_id is a non-empty string. Fix (separate PR, decoupled from the guard to avoid the guard+fix co-merge red): one shared BarkparkWeb.ErrorResponse.send(conn, reason) usable from both plugs and controllers, routing through Content.Errors.to_envelope/2; adopt it at the plug sites and retire the 4 private helpers. This is the 'collapse behind one emitter' the brief asked for, applied to the layer where the duplication actually remains.

action_fallback coverage: the 51 controllers without action_fallback either serve HTML / redirects (error_html, *_redirect, *_html) or deliberately own their JSON error path via a private helper that routes through Content.Errors (search, media, tickets_attachments). No controller drops an {:error, _} tuple on the floor.

Auth-plug halting discipline: every plug that emits an inline error envelope also calls halt() immediately after (require_user_session.ex:91, require_ingest_token.ex:66, optional_user_session.ex:76, github_webhook_signature.ex:58, require_principal_user.ex:30). No pipeline continues past a rejection.

Endpoint socket / check_origin: all four socket mounts (/live, /socket, /v1/plugins/pulse/socket, /quiz) deliberately inherit the endpoint-level check_origin allowlist with NO per-socket override, with inline comments citing Past-Mistake-#11 - the exact drift that made Studio click-dead. secure_session flips the cookie Secure flag at runtime without force_ssl (Golden Rule #5). Textbook-correct.

Router pipeline composition: 33 pipelines look large but are a tenancy/scope matrix (scoped_*, shared_*, require_*, ingest, github_webhook, media_mutate...). No dead or byte-identical duplicates surfaced; each variant carries a distinct plug set. Not a qualifying finding.

Body length cap: parse_body sets length: 100_000_000 for ALL parsers (json, urlencoded, multipart) at endpoint.ex:124. A per-parser split (cap JSON low, keep multipart high) is a plausible memory-amplification hardening, but there is already a RequestTooLargeError -> typed 413 path (endpoint.ex:141), and no measured RAM-pressure number backs a lower JSON cap. Rejected as speculative under the improvement doctrine - reopen with a measurement.

Verified routes (~p): the router uses plain-string paths (0 uses of ~p). Adopting verified routes across a 1929-line router is large churn with a weak failure mode (a broken route is a 404 caught by request tests). Modern-idiom rewrite with no named failure - rejected.

  missing_source not_intake runner_start_failed share_expired source_not_found unprocessable

Sites incl. bulldocs_ingest_controller.ex, status_controller.ex:62, ticket_keys_controller.ex:185,
github_adopt_controller.ex:76, self_update_controller.ex:29, access_controller.ex:188.

Protective test (fails today): assert every error code literal emitted by controllers on public /v1 routes is a member of Content.Errors.known_codes/0 (or on an explicit off-spec exclusion list for SCIM/OIDC/SAML). openapi_test.exs:220 only checks enum==known_codes; it does NOT check emitted-codes subset-of known_codes, so the drift is unguarded. Fix (separate PR): register the real public codes in @hints, or route those controllers through Content.Errors; add the subset guard so the class cannot reopen.

Finding 2 (ADOPT, P2): no single emitter - plug envelopes omit request_id - task-603d813e2d2b0b02

Named failure mode: the canonical envelope is documented as %{error: %{code, message, hint, request_id}} and built by Content.Errors, but the auth/pre-router plug layer (which has no action_fallback) hand-builds envelopes that OMIT request_id, then halt(). An anonymous caller hitting a 401/403 from an auth plug (e.g. a bad ingest token) gets a body with no request_id, so an operator cannot grep server logs to correlate the rejection - while the internal_error hint literally tells callers to 'report the request_id to the API operator' (errors.ex:44). Plug.RequestId already runs at endpoint.ex:74, so the id exists and is simply dropped. Secondarily, the envelope-build logic is forked into 4 private helpers - the exact sweep-the-tree scar.

Canonical envelope (error_json.ex:18):  %{error: %{code, message, hint, request_id}}
Owner Content.Errors.to_envelope/2 stamps hint + request_id (errors.ex:67-72, :329).
Plug.RequestId runs at endpoint.ex:74 (before router) -> request_id EXISTS in Logger metadata.

Auth/pre-router plugs (no action_fallback) hand-build envelopes WITHOUT request_id, then halt():
  require_user_session.ex:90    require_ingest_token.ex:65    optional_user_session.ex:75
  require_media_processing_callback_token.ex:28    require_principal_user.ex:28

Envelope-build logic is ALSO forked into 4 private copies (a contract change must edit all):
  search_controller.ex:342 error_json/3        v1/media_controller.ex:446 error_json/3
  tickets_attachments_controller.ex:317 enveloped/3 + :339 maybe_put_request_id/1
  endpoint.ex:153 parse_error_json/3

Protective test (fails today): drive an auth-plug rejection and assert body.error.request_id is a non-empty string. Fix (separate PR, decoupled from the guard to avoid the guard+fix co-merge red): one shared BarkparkWeb.ErrorResponse.send(conn, reason) usable from both plugs and controllers, routing through Content.Errors.to_envelope/2; adopt it at the plug sites and retire the 4 private helpers. This is the 'collapse behind one emitter' the brief asked for, applied to the layer where the duplication actually remains.

Already-good (first-class results, no task)

action_fallback coverage: the 51 controllers without action_fallback either serve HTML / redirects (error_html, *_redirect, *_html) or deliberately own their JSON error path via a private helper that routes through Content.Errors (search, media, tickets_attachments). No controller drops an {:error, _} tuple on the floor.

Auth-plug halting discipline: every plug that emits an inline error envelope also calls halt() immediately after (require_user_session.ex:91, require_ingest_token.ex:66, optional_user_session.ex:76, github_webhook_signature.ex:58, require_principal_user.ex:30). No pipeline continues past a rejection.

Endpoint socket / check_origin: all four socket mounts (/live, /socket, /v1/plugins/pulse/socket, /quiz) deliberately inherit the endpoint-level check_origin allowlist with NO per-socket override, with inline comments citing Past-Mistake-#11 - the exact drift that made Studio click-dead. secure_session flips the cookie Secure flag at runtime without force_ssl (Golden Rule #5). Textbook-correct.

Router pipeline composition: 33 pipelines look large but are a tenancy/scope matrix (scoped_*, shared_*, require_*, ingest, github_webhook, media_mutate...). No dead or byte-identical duplicates surfaced; each variant carries a distinct plug set. Not a qualifying finding.

Rejected-with-reason

Body length cap: parse_body sets length: 100_000_000 for ALL parsers (json, urlencoded, multipart) at endpoint.ex:124. A per-parser split (cap JSON low, keep multipart high) is a plausible memory-amplification hardening, but there is already a RequestTooLargeError -> typed 413 path (endpoint.ex:141), and no measured RAM-pressure number backs a lower JSON cap. Rejected as speculative under the improvement doctrine - reopen with a measurement.

Verified routes (~p): the router uses plain-string paths (0 uses of ~p). Adopting verified routes across a 1929-line router is large churn with a weak failure mode (a broken route is a 404 caught by request tests). Modern-idiom rewrite with no named failure - rejected.
